title: The Coast That Says No in Tongues

features.name: the pay-phone's long refusal
features.desc-on-touch: The receiver hangs at rest, having said no to every signal. You can hear salt in its yellow plastic, taste the years it chose not to speak.

features.name: the weatherboard shopfront
features.desc-on-touch: Its boards are nailed deliberate, the door a sealed fact. Inside, you can almost read the faded advertisement on the wall—once it promised something; now it promises nothing.

features.name: the tidal stone that learned its own answer
features.desc-on-touch: Grey, salt-bored, riddled with what waves asked. It says nothing back. Its refusal is older than speech.

features.name: the bell that learned to refuse its own sound
features.desc-on-touch: Mounted on a post, its clapper removed. The coastal wind passes through it without note. Its silence is its sharpest language.

features.name: the margin where speech learned its own evasion
features.desc-on-touch: Where the salt-dampened sand meets the boards, word-shapes emerge from the corroded metal plaques. They dissolve as you read them, never quite saying what they meant.

inscription: the coast has learned to say no in a thousand voices that refuse to translate

file.name: CoastalRefusals_VoiceRecordings_Fragmentary.mp3
file.note: Waves, wind, the bell that never rings, someone's voice starting to speak and stopping. The corruption has spliced in words from the shopfront's faded sign, making the waves say: I will not. I will no
